profile.source: Mario · Recorded DISC / Driving Forces / Acumen debrief

chapters.title: Welcome, Mario
chapters.text: Hi Mario, thank you for giving me the opportunity to debrief you on your assessment results. Let's look at how you behave, why you do what you do, and your acumen, which is how clearly you're thinking. There are two DISC graphs: Natural, how you behave at home, and Adapted, how you might modify your behavior in the workplace. Each graph runs from zero to 100, with the center at 50. Most of your colors are near the center. You're someone who's very adaptive and adaptable, depending on the situation.

chapters.title: DISC · Dominance and Influence
chapters.text:
Your red is D for Dominance: how you approach problems and challenges. People with high Dominance are urgent, task-oriented, and focused on getting the job done. They have high expectations of others and themselves. You could almost say D is for doers. Yours is 56 and 58. You're not always urgent or pushing for the next project. You're more circumspect than someone at 90 or 100. You tend to be mild-mannered, and you may get frustrated when people aren't responsive or responsible enough to meet your expectations. The emotion behind Dominance is frustration or anger. You may also get upset when you feel people are taking advantage of you. High D tells itself, 'I can conquer my environment.' You don't shy away from challenges. If you need to, you can be confrontational, strong, and debate with the best of them. Overall, I would put you as a mild Dominance, able to raise it or decrease it when you need to.

Your Influence is 72 at home and 64 in the workplace. This deals with people and contacts. You can articulate what you want to say, be verbal and optimistic, but you also need private time to pull back and recharge. Next to your Dominance, your optimism says, 'Yes, I can do this.' As much as you want to be with people and talk to people, you can also step away from the crowd. Creativity, innovation, marketing, and promoting things are important traits here. You drop Influence by eight points at work and raise Dominance from 56 to 58: less talkative and more action-based. Together, it's almost like a James Bond character, mixing charm with being decisive and action-oriented, on a mild level.

chapters.title: DISC · Pace, detail, and adaptability
chapters.text:
Green is Steadiness, which deals with pace and consistency. As green goes higher, pace slows and consistency increases. As it goes lower, the pace becomes faster. You can multitask when you need to. Near the center, especially at work, you're trying to be adaptive. If a task requires speed, you're able to do that. If it needs steady, careful consideration, you're able to see it through. You like some variety in your life. The emotion behind Steadiness is non-expression: as S rises, you tend to be less expressive; as it falls, you tend to be more emotionally expressive. Your steady pace depends on what you're doing.

Blue is Compliance: analysis, details, constraints, regulations, and doing things right. You're at 42 and 45. You pick where to be compliant and where to use more creativity. The emotion behind Compliance is fear or cautiousness. In your case, there are some things you're cautious about and some you're not. Sometimes you follow a steady progression as long as things make sense; sometimes you ask, 'What if we look at it from a different angle?'

As you and your partner launch a business, you can put your foot on the gas or on the brake. You can be creative, steady, fast, dominant, or non-confrontational. On the Success Insights wheel, you move between Persuading Promoter and Promoting Persuader: people and action. You're able to promote and communicate why you want to do something. When I put this next to your acumen, I see that you're able to start, withstand the long process, and finish. Congratulations: I hardly ever see this. You can take a project, be creative, think it through, strategize, and make it happen.

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Innovation, learning, and return
chapters.text:
Your drivers explain why you do the things you do. Your number one is Receptive, opposite Structured. Structured is old ways and practices; Receptive is innovation, change, and creativity. You're all about creating things, and this goes hand in hand with your persuasive profile.

Number two is Intellectual versus Instinctive. You like to study, learn, and understand the mechanics of things: how they work and how they're put together. Combined with Receptive, you study how to innovate and create things differently.

Number three is Resourceful. You want a return on your investment of time, money, and energy. You want to be efficient and effective. You don't want to waste time on things that aren't giving you ROI. You find an innovation, study it, and make sure it can make money and work efficiently.

Number four is Intentional versus Altruistic. You're purpose-driven and think strategically. Your brain almost doesn't stop: 'I'm going to create something. How do I do it?' If you hit a stumbling block, you research solutions. Then you ask, 'Does it make money? Is it efficient? What do I need to get it done?'

chapters.title: Driving Forces · Harmony and collaboration
chapters.text:
When we overlay your drivers with DISC, I see you doing exactly what you want to be doing. Your frustration may be that the return on investment isn't present yet.

Number five is Harmonious versus Objective. You enjoy aesthetically pleasing surroundings and how things feel. Overcoming a challenge can make you feel that things are happening. You don't like a lot of bickering or fighting.

With power, you can be Collaborative or Commanding. You don't have a problem leading, but you also prefer collaborating and getting things done with other people. There's no ego invested in getting things done.

chapters.title: Acumen · World View
chapters.text:
Your dimensional balance looks at people, tasks, systems, yourself, roles, and the future. For people, your clarity is 96. You can go anywhere, talk to anyone, and understand what makes people tick. The up-and-down arrow shows balance.

For tasks, your clarity is 92, again with an up-and-down arrow. You have no problem working with details. You think in practical terms and don't shy away from practical work.

For systems, your clarity is 92, with an up arrow. You can create systems and strategy, see the picture and its little dots, and enjoy doing it. Your brain works in systems. You're a big thinker. Your World View is powerful and clear, with a balanced, realistic perspective on performance and the situations around you. Your external emotional bias distortion is 7.

chapters.title: Acumen · Self View
chapters.text:
Your Sense of Self has clarity of 78, with a down arrow. It's like saying, 'I'm self-aware, but I'm not a finished product. There are still places on the canvas I need to paint. I need to learn, grow, and make life better for myself and the people around me.'

For the roles you're playing, at home and work, your clarity is 80, with an up-and-down arrow. You're practical and pragmatic about those roles. For the future, you have an up arrow: 'I know the future will be good.'

Internally, you have a balanced perspective on performance and situational awareness. Your emotional bias distortion is 24. You can be harder on yourself, take things personally, get down on yourself after a mistake, or overanalyze. My advice is to relax with it and let it go. You have excellent acumen. Your capacity for solving problems involving people, practical situations, theoretical situations, and decisions is outstanding, externally and internally, especially regarding your role.

chapters.title: Your outlook and next steps
chapters.text:
Your business performance summary shows balanced decision making at 82 against a global average of 70, and high concentration internally and externally. We say, 'If you're going to be successful, show up. If you're going to be really successful, show up with a good attitude.' Your Attitude Index is phenomenal: positive, encouraging, upbeat, appreciative, grateful, open-minded, flexible, approving, dynamic, and energetic.

The other part of your assessment is your 25 DNA soft skills. Your developmental indicators show where potential improvements could be, beginning on page 63 of your report. Overall, I would say you're exactly where you need to be. I like your clear-minded acumen, your drivers, and your DISC. The three together show someone powerful in mind and emotions, able to navigate hard times and come out on the other side. It's been great going over your profile. If you have any questions, I'm sure you'll let me know.
